translations.text: Psalm Forty-Three
I cried out to the Lord when I was oppressed in my extremity, and to God when sinners attacked me.
For suddenly the sound of battle was heard before me. He will hear me, for I was filled with righteousness.
And I thought in my heart that I was filled with righteousness, when I became rich and had many children.
For their wealth was given to the whole earth, and their glory reached to the ends of the earth.
They were raised up to the stars and said that they would not fall.
They [?] in their prosperity and did not understand.
For their sins were hidden; I did not know.
Their wrongdoing exceeded that of the nations before them, and they defiled the Lord’s temple with impurity.
Psalm Forty-Four
In his arrogance, the wicked man threw down fortified walls during the festival, and you did not restrain him.
Foreign nations went up onto your altar and arrogantly trampled it with their sandals.
For the people of Jerusalem had defiled the Lord’s sanctuary and were defiling God’s offerings with wrongdoing.
For this reason he said, “Remove them and cast them away from me.” And the beauty of his glory was not established among them.
It was rejected before the Lord and utterly disgraced.
Her sons and daughters were in bitter captivity, and the nations’ sealed yoke was placed on their necks.
He dealt with them according to their sins, for he abandoned them into the hands of someone stronger than they were.
For he turned his face away from his loved ones—the young, the old, and their children together.
For they too had done evil together, refusing to listen to me.
Heaven became exceedingly angry, and the earth rejected them.
For no human being upon it had done what they did.
And so that the earth might know that all your judgments are righteous, O God.
They set up Jerusalem’s sons within her to be mocked, in place of prostitutes. Everyone who passed by passed as though facing the sun, mocking their wrongdoing.
Just as they themselves used to do, they exposed their wrongdoing before the sun. And Jerusalem’s daughters were defiled in accordance with your judgments.
Because they had defiled themselves through promiscuous intercourse, my belly and my inward parts ache over these things.
But I declare you just, Lord, in the uprightness of my heart, for your righteousness is in your judgments, O God.
For you repay the wicked according to their deeds and according to their evil and bitter sins.
You exposed their sins so that your judgment might be known.
You wiped out their memory from the earth, O God, a righteous judge who shows no partiality.
For the nations reviled Jerusalem in their wickedness, and her beauty was cut off from her glorious throne.
She clothed herself in sackcloth instead of beautiful clothing, with a rope on her head instead of a crown.
She removed from herself the glorious splendor that God had placed upon her.
Her beauty was thrown to the ground in disgrace.
I saw this and sought the face of the Lord, and I said, “Enough! You have laid your hand heavily upon Israel, Lord, by bringing the nations against it.”
For they mocked and showed no mercy, in anger and rebuke.
They bring complete destruction unless you, Lord, rebuke them in your anger.
For they did not act out of zeal, but out of their own desire,
to pour out their anger upon us by plundering. But you, Lord, do not delay; repay them upon their own heads,
to cast down the dragon’s arrogance in disgrace.
I did not have to wait long before the Lord showed me his disgrace: he lay struck down on the mountains of Egypt, more despised than the lowliest on land and sea.
And his body came upon the waves in great disgrace, with no one to bury it.
For he rejected him in disgrace. For he had not considered that he was a human being, nor had he thought about his end.
For he said, “I will be lord of the earth and the sea,” and he did not know that the Lord is God, great, strong, and mighty,
And he is king over heaven and earth, and he judges kingdoms and rulers.
who raises me up in glory and lays the arrogant low in disgrace, not for a time but forever, because they did not know him.
Now, rulers of the earth, see the judgment of the Lord, for he is a righteous king and judges everything beneath heaven.
Bless the Lord, you who fear the Lord in due form, for the Lord’s mercy is upon those who fear him when he judges,
To distinguish between the righteous and the wicked, to repay the wicked forever according to their deeds.
to spare the righteous from the humiliation inflicted by the wicked, and to repay the wicked for violating righteousness.
For the Lord is kind to those who call upon him with patient endurance, acting according to his mercy toward his faithful ones, so that they may always stand firmly before him.
Blessed be the Lord forever by his servants.
Songs of forty-five.
Why are you sleeping, my soul, and not blessing the Lord?
Sing a new song of praise to God, and awaken at his awakening, for a psalm to God from a good heart is good.
Let the righteous always remember the Lord, with thanksgiving and with the righteousness of the Lord’s judgments.
The righteous person who is disciplined by the Lord does not become careless, for his will is always before the Lord.
The righteous person stumbles and acknowledges that God is just. He falls and waits to see what the Lord will do for him.
He watches to see where his deliverance will come from.
The steadfastness of the righteous comes from God their Savior. For sin upon sin does not lodge in the house of the righteous.
For the righteous person constantly examines his house to remove the sins of his lapses.
Through fasting and humility he redeems himself from whatever sins he has committed unknowingly.
The Lord cleanses every devout person and his household.
But the wicked person stumbles and curses his life, the day on which he was born, and his mother's labor pains.
He adds sins upon sins throughout his life.
He falls, and because his fall is disastrous, he will not rise. For the destruction of the wicked person lasts forever.
He will not be remembered when God attends to the righteous.
This is the portion of the wicked forever.
But those who fear the Lord will rise to everlasting life. Their life is in the light of the Lord, and it will never again perish. Hallelujah!
Song Forty-Seven.
Why do you, wicked person, sit in the assembly of the righteous, while your heart is far from God? By your wrongdoing you provoke the God of Israel to anger.
Especially in your words, and especially in your signs, more than anyone—the one who is harsh in his words, condemning sinners in judgment.
His hand is the first raised against him, as though out of zeal, yet he himself is guilty of the great excesses of sinners.
His eyes are on every woman without modesty, and his tongue lies by twisting oaths.
At night and in darkness, as though unseen, he speaks with his eyes to every woman with evil cunning.
He is quick to enter every house cheerfully, as though there were no evil in him.
Remove, O God, those who judge with corrupt partiality yet live among the upright, through the wasting of their bodies and the impoverishment of their lives.
May God expose the deeds of those who seek to please people; may his deeds become an object of laughter and mockery.
May the devout acknowledge the justice of their God's judgment when the wicked are removed from the presence of the righteous.
The hypocrite speaks of the law deceitfully.
His eyes are on the house, silently like a snake, to undermine each person's wisdom with words of wrongdoing.
His words are formed with evil intent, to fulfill a desire for wrongdoing.
And he did not stop until he scattered the household [?] and ruined the house because of his wicked desire.
And he thought to himself that there was no one who saw and judged.
And he was filled with this wickedness, and his eyes were on another house, to ruin it with licentious words. Like Sheol, his soul is not satisfied with all these things.
May his portion from the Lord be dishonor before you, his going out accompanied by groans and his coming in by curses.
Lord, may his life be spent in pain, poverty, and deprivation, his sleep in distress and his waking in rebukes.
May sleep be removed from his temples at night. May he fail disgracefully in all the work of his hands.
May he enter his house empty-handed, and may his house lack everything that satisfies the soul.
May not one of his children come near him.
May the flesh of those who show favoritism be scattered by wild animals, and the bones of the wicked lie dishonored before the sun.
May ravens peck out the eyes of those who seek to please people.
For they have disgracefully ruined many people's houses and scattered them in their greed.
They did not remember God, nor did they fear God in any of these things.
They provoked God, and he became angry enough to destroy them from the earth, because with perverse intent they ingratiated themselves with innocent souls.
Blessed are those who fear the Lord in their integrity.
May the Lord save them from deceitful and wicked men, and may he save us from every stumbling block set by the wicked.
Destroy, O God, all who arrogantly commit oppression, for the Lord our God is a mighty judge who judges righteously.
Lord, may your mercies be upon all who love you.
Song Forty-eight
Lord my God, I will praise your name with joy among those who know your righteous judgments.
For you are kind and merciful, and a refuge for the poor.
When I cry out to you, do not remain silent toward me.
For a person does not take captives from a mighty man.
Or who can receive anything you have made unless you give it to him?
For a person and his allotted portion are weighed before you, and he cannot gain anything beyond your judgment, O God.
In our distress we called upon you to help us, and you did not turn away our petition, because you are our God.
Do not withhold your hand from us, lest we grow bold enough to sin.
Do not turn your face away from us, lest we stray far from you; rather, let us come to you.
For if I am hungry, Lord, I will call to you, God, and you will give.
For you sustain the birds and the fish, giving rain in the wilderness to make grass grow and to prepare food in the wilderness for every animal.
And if they are hungry, they will lift their faces to you.
You are the one who feeds kings, rulers, and nations, God. And who is the hope of the poor and the afflicted, if not you, Lord?
You will answer him because you are kind and gentle, and you will satisfy his soul when you open your hand to him in mercy.
For human generosity is grudging, today and tomorrow. And if someone gives again, he grumbles—and even this is remarkable.
But your giving is abundant in generosity and wealth, and whoever hopes in you will not lack gifts.
For your mercies, Lord, extend graciously over the whole earth.
Blessed is the person whom you remember, Lord, in his poverty.
For a person may become rich enough to sin against him.
Poverty with righteousness is beneficial.
For those who fear the Lord have enjoyed his good things, and your favor rests upon Israel in your kingdom.
Blessed is the praise of the Lord, because he is our king.
Song Forty-Nine
Blessed is the person who prepares his heart to call upon the name of the Lord.
When he remembers the name of the Lord, he will be saved.
His paths are made straight before the Lord, and the works of his hands are protected by his God.
Evil sees him in the night but will not disturb him [?], because he belongs to him.
And his soul will not be alarmed when crossing rivers or amid the turmoil of the seas.
For he rose from his sleep and praised the name of the Lord.
With a peaceful heart he sang to the name of the Lord and prayed before the Lord for his entire household.
The Lord hears the prayer of everyone who fears him, and the Lord fulfills every request of the soul that hopes in him.
Blessed is he who shows mercy to those who truly love him.
Song Fifty
Do not move your dwelling far from us, God, lest those who hate us without cause rise against us.
For you have driven them back, God, so that their feet will not trample your holy inheritance.
Discipline us according to your will, and do not hand us over to the nations.
For if you send death, you yourself bring it upon us, because you are merciful. Do not be angry enough to destroy us completely.
For the sake of your name, which dwells among us, let mercy be shown to us.
Do not let the nations gain strength against us, because you are our strength.
We will cry out to you, and you will answer us.
For you will show favor to the descendants of Israel forever and will not forget them.
Prepare us in the time of your help, to show favor to the house of Jacob on that day which is prepared for them.
Song Fifty-One
My ears heard distress and the sound of war—the sound of war and the uproar of slaughter and destruction.
The sound of a vast people was like a strong, mighty wind, like a whirlwind of fire coming over the wilderness.
And I said to myself, “Where, then, will he judge him?”
I heard a voice in Jerusalem, the holy city.
The joints of my back came loose at the report, and my knees trembled.
My bones shook like flax.

And I said, “Let them set their paths straight in righteousness.” I remembered the Lord’s judgments from the time heaven and earth were created, and I declared God righteous in all his judgments from ancient times.
But God revealed their deeds in the sunlight, and the Lord’s righteous judgments became known to the whole earth.
For they were committing wickedness in the hidden places of the land.
A son was having intercourse with his mother, and a father with his daughter.
They were all committing adultery with their neighbors’ wives, and they made agreements among themselves about these things.
They were plundering God’s sanctuary as though there were no one to inherit or redeem it.
They were trampling his temple with all their uncleanness, and with menstrual blood they defiled the sacrifices as though they were unclean meat.
They left no sin uncommitted, and they sinned more than the nations.
For this reason God mixed a spirit of error for them and made them drink an undiluted cup to make them drunk.
He brought the one from the ends of the earth who oppresses harshly.
And he waged war against Jerusalem and its land.
The judges of the land welcomed him joyfully and said to him, “Your way will be prepared. Come, enter in peace.”
And they leveled the uneven roads for his entrance. They opened the gates of Jerusalem and crowned its walls.
And he entered peacefully, like a father entering his children's house, and planted his feet very firmly.
And they seized Jerusalem's towers and walls.
For God was in control of their deception.
And they destroyed their rulers, because he is wise in counsel. And they poured out the blood of Jerusalem's inhabitants like filthy water.
And he led away their sons and daughters, those who were in a state of impurity.
And they practiced their impurity, just as their fathers had.
And Jerusalem defiled even those who sanctified the name of God.
And God was vindicated in his judgments among the nations of the earth.
And God's faithful ones were like unblemished lambs among them.
Praised is God, who judges the whole earth in his righteousness.
See, you, God, have shown us your righteousness.
And our eyes have seen your judgments, God, and we have acknowledged your honored name as righteous forever.
For you are the God of righteousness, who judges Israel through discipline.
Turn your mercy toward us and be gracious to us.
And gather the scattered people of Israel with mercy and grace.
For your faithfulness is with us. We are stubborn, and you are the one who disciplines us.
Do not hold back from us, our God, lest the nations swallow us up as though there were no one to rescue us.
And you have been our God from the beginning, and our hope is in you, Lord.
And we will not depart from you, because your judgments are good.
May your favor be upon us and upon our children forever, Lord God our Savior, and we will never again be shaken.
The Lord is praised for his judgments by the mouths of his faithful ones, and Israel is blessed by the Lord forever.
The fifty-second song.
When Israel went into captivity in a foreign land, when they departed from the Lord their Savior.
They were cast out of the inheritance that God had given them. Israel was scattered among all the nations, according to God's word.
So that you, God, may be vindicated in your righteousness through our wrongdoing.
For you are the righteous judge over all the nations of the earth.
For no one who does wrong is hidden from your mind.
But the righteousness of your upright ones, Lord, is before you. Where can a human being hide from your mind, God?
For we act freely and by our own choice, doing good and evil through the work of our hands.
And in your righteousness you watch over human beings.
For whoever practices righteousness stores up a treasure of life for himself with the Lord. But whoever does wrong brings a sentence of destruction upon his own soul.
For his judgments are righteous against every person and his household.
For to whom will God show kindness, except those who call upon the Lord?
For he cleanses the soul's sins through confession.
For shame is upon us and upon our faces because of all these things.
For whose sins will he forgive, except those who have sinned?
For you bless the righteous, and you do not rebuke them for anything in which they have sinned. For your grace rests upon those who have sinned when they repent.

And now you are our God, and we are your people whom you have loved. Look and have mercy, God of Israel, because we belong to you. Do not withdraw your mercy from us, so that the nations do not attack us.
For you chose Abraham's descendants above all the nations.
And you placed your name upon us, Lord. Do not cease forever.
You established a covenant with our ancestors concerning us, and we hope in you as our souls repent.
For mercy toward the house of Israel belongs to the Lord, now and forever.
Song Fifty-Three
Blessed is the man whom God remembers with rebuke and restrains from the path of evil with lashes, to cleanse him from his sin so that it does not increase.
For whoever prepares his back for lashes will also be cleansed. For he is good to those who accept discipline.
For the path of the righteous is straight, and discipline does not lead him astray.
For the Lord's gaze is upon those who truly love him, and the Lord will remember his servants with mercy.
For there is testimony in the law of the everlasting covenant: the Lord's testimony concerning the ways of human beings in their deeds.
Our God is righteous and upright in all his judgments, and Israel will praise the Lord's name with joy.
And the faithful will give thanks in the assembly of the people, and the Lord will have mercy on the poor as he brings comfort to Israel.
For God is kind and merciful forever, and the congregations of Israel will praise the Lord's name.
For salvation for the house of Israel belongs to the Lord, for an everlasting kingdom.
Song Fifty-[?]
Sound the horn in Zion as a signal to the holy ones.
Proclaim in Jerusalem the voice of those who bring good news, for God has shown mercy to Israel by coming to their aid.
Stand on the heights, Jerusalem, and see your children, all gathered from east and west by the Lord.
From the north they come to rejoice in their God, and from distant islands God has gathered them.
He humbled the high mountains and brought them low.
The hills fled as they approached. Cedars shaded them as they passed.
God made every sweet-smelling tree give off its fragrance for them, so that Israel might pass through as their God came to them in glory.
Put on your glorious garments, Jerusalem, and prepare the robe of your holiness, for God has spoken good things for Israel, now and forever.
May the Lord do what he has spoken concerning Israel and Jerusalem. May the Lord establish Israel by his glorious name. The Lord's mercies are upon Israel now and forever.
Song fifty-five.
Lord, rescue my soul from the perverse and unjust man, and from the slanderous, lawless tongue that speaks lies and deceit.
For the tongue of a lawless man twists words. He presents himself as someone who does good, while he sets fire among the people.
For he lives to fill houses with lying speech. He cuts down the trees of his delight with the fire of a lawbreaker.
Destroy the houses of lawbreakers in war, and keep slanderous lips far from the blameless, O God—the lips of lawbreakers. May the bones of slanderers be scattered far from those who fear the Lord.
May the slanderous tongue perish in blazing fire, far from the upright and their homes.
May the Lord protect the righteous, whose soul hates evildoers. May the Lord guide the man who makes peace in the Lord's house.
For the Lord is salvation for Israel his servant forever.
May sinners perish together before the Lord, and may the Lord's faithful ones inherit the Lord's promises.
Song fifty-six.
The Lord's right hand has sheltered us. The Lord's right hand has had compassion on us.
The Lord's arm has rescued us from the spear that roams about, and from the famine and plague of sinners.
He sent wild beasts rushing against them. They tore their flesh with their teeth and crushed their bones with their molars. But the Lord rescued us from all these things.
But the wicked man trembled because of his missteps, lest he be shattered along with the evildoer.
For the evildoer's downfall is terrible, but not one of these things will come near the righteous.
For the discipline of the righteous for unintentional wrongdoing cannot be compared with the destruction of evildoers.
with understanding. For the righteous person is disciplined so that the wicked person may not rejoice over him.
For he will admonish the righteous person as his beloved son, and discipline him as a firstborn son.
For the Righteous One will have mercy on his faithful ones and wipe away their failings through discipline. For the lives of the righteous endure forever.
But sinners will be swept away to destruction, and their memory will no longer be found.
But the Lord's mercy will be upon the faithful; he will shelter all who fear him.
Song Fifty-Seven
The Lord is faithful to those who truly love him, to those who endure his discipline, to those who walk righteously in his commandments. He gave us a law for our lives.
And the Lord's faithful ones will live by it forever. The Lord's paradise consists of trees of life, which are his faithful ones.
Their planting is firmly established forever, and they will not be uprooted as long as the heavens endure. For Israel is the Lord's portion and inheritance.
Not so the sinners and the wicked, who loved a day in the company of sin. For their desire is for the brief span of evil.
And they did not remember God, before whom the ways of human beings are always revealed. He knows the inner chambers of the heart before they come into being.
Therefore their inheritance is Sheol, destruction, and darkness. On the day of mercy for the righteous, they will not be found. For the Lord's faithful ones will inherit life in delight.
Song Fifty-Eight
In my distress I called on the Lord's name. I called on the God of Jacob to help me, and I was saved.
For you, God, are the hope and refuge of the poor.
For who is strong enough to give you thanks in truth?
And what strength does a human being have, except to give thanks to your name?
A new song, sung aloud with gladness of heart; the fruit of lips, with an instrument tuned by the tongue; the firstfruits of lips from a faithful and righteous heart.
Anyone who does these things will never be shaken by evil. The fiery flame and the wrath against the wicked will not come near them,
when it goes out against sinners from the presence of the Most High, to uproot all the roots of the wicked.
For the Lord's sign is upon the righteous for salvation. Death, the spear, and famine will stay far from the righteous.

For they will flee from them as death flees from life. But they will pursue the wicked and overtake them. Those who practice wickedness will not escape the Lord's judgments, for like seasoned warriors they will intercept them.
For the sign of destruction is upon their faces.
The inheritance of sinners is destruction and darkness, and their wickedness will pursue them down to the lowest Sheol.
And their inheritance will not be found for their children.
For their sins will lay waste the houses of sinners, and sinners will perish forever on the day of the Lord's judgment,
when God visits the earth in judgment.
Mercy will be upon those who fear the Lord. In it they will live through the compassion of our God, but sinners will perish forever.
Song Fifty-Nine
When I neglected my soul a little, away from the Lord, I nearly slipped into the sleep of destruction.
When I went far from the Lord, my soul was nearly poured out into death beside the gates of Sheol, among sinners.
And when my soul turned away from the God of Israel, had the Lord not helped me in his everlasting mercy—
He prodded me as a horse is spurred to awaken it. He who is always my savior and helper gave me life.
I will thank you, God, because you helped me through your salvation and did not count me among the sinners destined for destruction.
Do not take your mercy far from me, God, and do not let the remembrance of you depart from my heart until death.
Save me, Lord, from evil sin and from every wicked woman who makes the inexperienced stumble.
Do not let the beauty of a wicked woman make me stumble, nor any sin whatsoever.
Establish the work of my hands before you, and keep my steps in remembrance of you.
Set my tongue and my lips right with words of truth. Keep anger and groundless rage far from me.
Keep grumbling and faintheartedness in distress far from me. For if I sin while you discipline me to bring me to repentance,
strengthen my soul with joyful willingness. And when you strengthen my soul, let what is given be enough for me.
For if you do not strengthen me, who can endure discipline in poverty?
When the soul wastes away in his flesh and in the distress of his poverty.
When a righteous person endures these things, mercy from the Lord will be upon him.
Song Sixty
Lord, you are our king, now and forever, for our soul will boast in you, God.
What is the life of a human being on earth? For as his allotted time is, so also is his flesh.
But we place our hope in God our savior, because the dominion of our God lasts forever in mercy.
The kingdom of our God is forever over the nations in judgment.
You, Lord, chose David as king over Israel, and you swore to him concerning his offspring that their kingdom would not cease before you.
But because of our sins, sinners rose against us. They set upon us and drove me away—those whom you had not commanded. They took by force.
They did not praise your glorious name with songs of praise, but established a kingdom for their own exaltation.
They destroyed David’s throne in the arrogance of their usurpation. But you will overthrow them and remove their offspring from the earth.
And when a foreign man from our own lineage rises against them,
Repay them according to their sins, O God, and deal with them according to their deeds.
Do not have mercy on them, O God. Punish their descendants, and do not leave even one of them.
The Lord is faithful in all the judgments he has carried out on earth.
The wicked one devastated our land, leaving it without inhabitants. They destroyed children and old people and their sons together.
In the splendor of his anger he sent them away as far as the west, to the end of the earth, to be mocked, and he did not spare them.
In a foreign land the enemy boasts, and his heart is estranged from our God.
Jerusalem did everything that the nations also did in their cities for their gods.
The children of the covenant were held captive among the mixed nations, and there was no one among them who practiced mercy and truth in Jerusalem.
Those who loved the congregation of the faithful fled from them and flew away like birds flying from their nests.
They wandered in the wilderness to save their lives from evil. Precious in their eyes was the temporary dwelling of the life that was being rescued from them.
They were scattered throughout the whole earth because of the wicked. Therefore the heavens were shut so that they would not send rain down upon the earth.

And the age-old springs were shut off, from the depths and from the high mountains, because there was no one among them who practiced righteousness and justice. From their rulers down to their least, they were involved in every kind of sin.
The king acts wickedly, the judge provokes anger, and the people live in sin.
Look, Lord, and raise up for them their king, the son of David, at the time you see fit, O God, to reign over Israel your servant.
Strengthen him with power to humble wicked rulers,
so that he may cleanse Jerusalem of the nations that trample it to destruction,
to destroy the wicked from your inheritance, to crush arrogance like a potter's vessel, to crush all their strength with an iron rod,
to destroy wicked nations by the word of his mouth. At his rebuke the nations will flee from his presence, and he will rebuke sinners with a word directed at their hearts.
He will gather a holy people who will take pride in righteousness, and he will judge the tribes of the people whom the Lord his God sanctifies.
He will no longer allow sin to dwell [?] among them, nor will anyone who knows evil live among them anymore.
For he knows them, because they are all children of God, and he will distribute them in the land according to their tribes.
No temporary resident or foreigner will live with them, because he judges peoples and nations with the wisdom of his righteousness.
He will acquire a people from the nations to serve him under his yoke, and they will praise the Lord openly throughout the whole earth.
He will cleanse Jerusalem in holiness as in former times,
so that nations may come from the ends of the earth to see his glory, bringing honor to her children who were scattered from her,
and to see the glory of the Lord, with which God has glorified her. And he is a righteous king, taught by God, over them.
There is no wrongdoing among them in his days, because they are all holy, and their king is the Lord’s Messiah.
For he does not rely on a horse or its rider, or on a bow. Nor does he accumulate gold and silver for warfare, or rely on large numbers on the day of battle.
For the Lord, his king, is his hope, and his strength rests on hope in his God. And [?] over them all in fear.
For he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth forever.
And he will bless the Lord’s people with wisdom and delight.
And he purifies a great people from [?] the beginning, to rebuke rulers and destroy sinners by his word.
And in his days he will lack nothing from his God, because he is holy and wise in discerning counsel, in strength and righteousness.
And the Lord’s blessing is with him in power.
And he will not grow weak. His hope is in the Lord, and who can stand against him? For he is mighty in his deeds and strong in the fear of his God.
He shepherds the Lord’s flock in righteousness and faithfulness, and he will not allow anyone to grow weak in his flock.
He will gather them all in peace, and no arrogance will be found among them to overpower them.
This is the splendor of the king of Israel: to stand over the house of Israel and discipline it.
His words are more thoroughly refined than gold, and precious in assemblies, to distinguish the tribes of the holy people.
His words are like the words of holy ones among the holy people.
Blessed are those who live in those days, to see the good things of Israel in the assembly of the people that God has made,
to hasten his mercies toward Israel, so that they may escape the uncleanness of the defiled nations. For the Lord is our king, now and forever.
Lord, your mercies are upon the work of your hands forever.
And your goodness is bestowed in a rich gift upon Israel. Your eyes see everything, and nothing is hidden from them.
And your ears listen to the poor person’s hope. Your judgments are over the whole earth in mercy.
And your love is upon the offspring of Israel, Abraham’s son. Your discipline is upon us as upon a firstborn and only son,
to turn back an obedient soul that has neither instruction nor knowledge,
to purify Israel for his day with blessing, for his day of election.
Blessed are those who live in those days, to see.
